description: Aesop configuration. Precedence: environment variables > config file > built-in defaults.

_paths.aesop_root: Set via AESOP_ROOT env var (no config key)
_paths.brain_root: Override via BRAIN_ROOT env var or config; default: {aesop_root}/../.claude
_paths.scripts_root: Override via SCRIPTS_ROOT env var or config; default: {aesop_root}/../scripts
_paths.temp_root: Override via TEMP_ROOT env var or config; default: system temp + /claude
_paths.state_root: Override via AESOP_STATE_ROOT env var or config; default: {aesop_root}/state
_paths.fleet_root: Override via AESOP_FLEET_ROOT env var or config; default: $HOME. SECURITY: all repository clone targets must remain under fleet_root to prevent credential harvesting across account boundaries. The monitor validates clone targets on each cycle and surfaces violations as HIGH alerts.
_paths.transcripts_root: Override via AESOP_TRANSCRIPTS_ROOT env var or config; default: ~/.claude/projects

_temp_root_notes: Portable path for temporary aesop files. ~ expands to home directory on both Windows and POSIX. Alternatively, on Windows set to %TEMP%/aesop, on POSIX set to /tmp/aesop. Config loaders expand ~ at runtime.
_fleet_root_note: SECURITY BOUNDARY: all repository clone targets must remain under fleet_root to prevent credential harvesting across account boundaries. The monitor validates clone targets on each cycle. Defaults to home directory if not specified.

seats._comment: Unified two-seat model selection (0.4.0). ONE block swaps BOTH seats: 'worker' = the coding agents (AgentDriver), 'orchestrator' = the decision seat (OrchestratorBackend). The values below ARE the defaults -- Claude Code worker + live-harness orchestrator -- so this block as shipped changes nothing; deleting it changes nothing either. To swap a seat, replace its block with one of the _worker_examples/_orchestrator_examples. Keys are read from env vars named by api_key_env at CALL time, never stored in this file. 'is_local': true = LOOPBACK endpoint only (localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 -- rejected otherwise): no API key needed, honest verification tier 3. Separate surface: cardinal_rules.subagent_model (above) pins the model for LIVE-HARNESS Claude Code subagents; seats.worker swaps the AgentDriver worker seam itself.

_worker_examples._note: Asymmetry: worker openai-compatible seats REQUIRE base_url; the orchestrator seat may omit base_url (defaults to the hosted OpenAI endpoint).

multibox._comment: Multi-instance coordination (Phase 0.5). The values below ARE the built-in defaults, so this block as shipped changes nothing and deleting it changes nothing: enabled=false means NO multibox code path is reached at all (tools/multibox_config.py returns before importing a single coordination module). Every key is overridable by an AESOP_MULTIBOX_<UPPER_KEY> environment variable; precedence is env > this file > default. Setting enabled=true runs a HARD startup preflight (tools/multibox_preflight.py) that REFUSES to proceed unless (i) the event-store SQLite DB is on local storage -- SQLite WAL needs a shared-memory index that is only coherent on one host, so a WAL DB on NFS/SMB is silently unsafe -- (ii) the measured p99 cross-box directory-visibility delay is below settle_seconds, and (iii) the measured clock skew is below max_skew_seconds. Probe failure is itself a refusal: an unmeasurable share is an unsafe share. The refusal message names the mount options that make a share measurable (NFS: nfsvers=4.1,actimeo=1,lookupcache=none / SMB: cache=none).
multibox._transport: 'local' = one box, atomic SQLite leases (LocalLeaseBackend) -- closes the multi_dispatch TOCTOU window without any shared filesystem. 'shared-fs' = 3-5 boxes sharing ONE directory (shared_dir) that carries only an append-only claim log; each instance keeps its own local SQLite event store. shared_dir is required for 'shared-fs' and forbidden for 'local' (a silently ignored share is a footgun).
multibox._tuning: settle_seconds must exceed the MEASURED p99 visibility delay -- it is the window a claim waits before folding the directory listing, and it is what makes a fold-decided claim safe (tools/verify_multibox.py proves it load-bearing by showing the same harness DOES double-grant when delay > settle). max_skew_seconds only ever LENGTHENS a lease, so over-estimating costs throughput, never correctness. heartbeat_seconds must stay below lease_ttl_seconds or a live instance's lease expires between heartbeats. case_policy='insensitive' deliberately over-collides across heterogeneous boxes: a spurious conflict costs throughput, a missed conflict costs correctness. instance_id=null derives a durable id from $AESOP_STATE_ROOT/instance-id.

limits._comment: Cost ceiling / kill switch (tools/cost_ceiling.py, tools/halt.py). null disables a given ceiling (feature opt-in). When spend meets or exceeds a configured ceiling, cost_ceiling.py trips tools/halt.py's .HALT sentinel, which daemons/run-watchdog.sh checks at the top of every cycle and refuses to do work (no backup, no push, no scan) until cleared via 'python tools/halt.py --clear'.

alerts._comment: Slack/Discord webhook integration for fleet alerts. webhook_url: null (default) disables alerts (feature opt-in). SETUP: (1) Slack: Create an app at https://api.slack.com/apps, enable 'Incoming Webhooks', add a new webhook to your channel, copy the Webhook URL. (2) Discord: In your Discord server, go to Server Settings > Integrations > Webhooks, create a webhook, copy its URL. SECURITY: NEVER commit a real webhook URL to version control — retrieve at runtime via environment variable AESOP_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_URL or load from a .env.local file. Provider: 'slack' (block-kit format) or 'discord' (embed format). min_severity: filter by HIGH/CRITICAL/etc. heartbeat_stall_s: alert if watchdog heartbeat older than N seconds (null = skip).
